disposition: User stopped the print after first-layer non-adherence and lifted material; failed material removed and bed cleared for retry.
source: Derek's observations and three photographs captured before peeling the failed print off the plate.
founder_quotes: Oh interesting,  we do have a failure on the current print, one of the inner Wall layers did not adhere and got lifted up at some point. I've stopped the print.
That was really more about the PETGF and probably shouldn't apply to the PETG if we're using that here.

Those photos were from that last print before I peeled it off the plate. Maybe you can see what I'm talking about with that non-adherence. But in any case, Mark One is clear now and ready for us to start the next print with at least that first layer Z offset removed, and potentially something else if you have a good something else to bring me at this point.
photo_observations: Photo 1 shows a loose raised strand at the cap perimeter beside the semicircular cutout; adjacent first-layer lines have visible separations.
Photo 2 shows the same cap region and the separate reservoir floor. Clear PETG reflections limit assessment of individual bead contact.
Photo 3 locates the cap on the left and body on the right. These still images do not establish when the strand first detached or establish later corner-warp onset.
diagnostic_scope: First-layer adhesion failure is reported and visible. Excess nozzle height is consistent with separated lines and the added trim; a photo does not isolate every possible cause. Earlier reservoir corner lifting is a separate reported observation with unverified timing.
retry: Zero added user Z trim for this clear PETG recipe, retaining stock Textured PEI -0.02 mm compensation and all other physical process settings; start A2 with automatic refill.
